title: Quality and Perception of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Content on TikTok: Cross-Sectional Study
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of the 125 most-liked English-language #adhd TikTok videos (searched 28-29 November 2023). Three raters classified each video as misleading, personal experience or useful against the German S3 ADHD guideline and ICD-11; 50.4% (63/125) were misleading. Because the numerator requires false or overgeneralising claims judged against an external clinical ground truth, this is CONTENT rather than QUALITY: a wholly accurate video could not receive the 'misleading' label. The separate PEMAT-A/V understandability and actionability scores are quality measures reported only as means, so they generate no row.

estimates.measure_type: % of the most-liked #adhd TikTok videos rated misleading
estimates.denominator: 125 English-language TikTok videos tagged #adhd, drawn from the 130 most-liked results and retained after exclusion criteria
estimates.definition: Video contained false information on ADHD, showed symptoms not typical for ADHD per the German S3 guideline and ICD-11, or made overgeneralising statements (e.g. 'everybody with this symptom has ADHD'); included videos claiming to provide a diagnostic test for ADHD

estimates.page_loc: Results, Usefulness and Quality of Videos, p. 5
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Three members of an interdisciplinary research group (a physician, a clinical psychologist and health-science researchers) rated each video independently against the German S3 ADHD guideline and ICD-11; disagreements resolved by discussion; inter-rater agreement moderate, kappa = 0.529 (P<.001)
estimates.moderator_quote: We searched the TikTok mobile app on November 28, 2023, and November 29, 2023, with the hashtag "#adhd" for videos about ADHD. The results were sorted for likes count, with the most popular videos (the videos receiving the most "likes") displayed at the top of the search.
estimates.notes: Rank-truncated hashtag corpus (top-130 by likes), hence denom_selection=curated. The 'misleading' category is broad: it merges factually false symptom claims with overgeneralisation, so breadth is coded misleading rather than false. Videos could be assigned to only one of the three categories, so the categories are mutually exclusive but not summable into anything else useful.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) PEMAT-A/V understandability (mean 79.5%) and actionability (mean 5.1%) scores — these are quality/comprehensibility scores reported as means, not shares of items judged false, so no row per the instructions; (b) the comment-level content categories (e.g. 'self-attribution of behavioural patterns' 220/600, 36.7%; self-diagnosis shares by video category) — these count viewer reactions in comments, not misinformation in the comments, so they are not a prevalence estimate; (c) the 52% misleading figure cited from Yeung et al is a figure the paper cites from elsewhere (barred by R8); (d) creator/video descriptive shares (84% English-speaking country of origin, 38.4% United States) are not misinformation measures. Judgement call: the 50.4% could be argued into QUALITY because the coding label also covers overgeneralisation, but overgeneralised claims of the stated form ('everybody with this symptom has ADHD') are themselves false statements and a wholly accurate video would not be labelled misleading, so CONTENT is the correct construct.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. 130 most-liked #adhd TikTok videos scraped 28-29 November 2023 (Apify), 125 retained after exclusions (non-English, pre-19 July 2021, no audio or text, comments disabled, advertising, other conditions). Three raters classified usefulness independently against the German S3 guideline and ICD-11, disagreements resolved by discussion, kappa = 0.529. Quality assessed with PEMAT-A/V by two raters independently. Comment analysis on a purposive sample of 6 videos, 100 random comments each (600 comments).
rob.item6_quote: Videos were considered misleading if they contained false information on ADHD and if they showed symptoms not considered typical for ADHD (based on the German S3 guideline on ADHD and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision)
rob.item10_quote: Of the 125 included videos, 50.4% (63/125) of videos were rated misleading, 30.4% (38/125) showed a personal experience, and 19.2% (24/125) were useful.
